$comment: Two kinds, and the distinction is the point. `wcag-exempt` means the
success criterion does not apply — the pairing is correct and will never
need fixing. `defect` means it genuinely fails and is not fixed yet; the
gate keeps reporting those in its summary so they cannot be forgotten,
and they are copied into every affected component's contract as
a11y.knownIssues so a consumer is told before they ship it.
An exception that no longer fails is itself an error. Otherwise this file
$deferredModesComment: No mode is deferred. Dark was, from 18 Aug to 4 Sep 2026, while the dark theme
was still being designed — see git history for the reasoning, which was sound:
measuring a theme mid-design produced findings that were true of that day's
values and were being shipped into component contracts on npm.
It was un-deferred once the five real Dark defects were fixed at source in Figma
and the gate reported '0 without an exemption'. The fix was not five fixes: three
accent text roles were sitting on the /400 rung where error and information had
already moved to /300, and the purple ramp did not hold its slot at /400 or /500 —
it was the only ramp of eight whose luminance fell outside its siblings' range at
those rungs. Re-rung the three, lifted the two purple steps, done.
To defer a mode again, put its name back in deferredModes. The gate will measure
it, print it, and stop failing on it — and stop writing it into any contract.

accepted.reason: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component: it has no contrast requirement. Disabled controls are required to look unavailable, and raising this would work against that.

Not a text pairing. `.ion-confidence__bar--on` is an empty, aria-hidden <span> — the gate pairs the inherited text colour against its background because it models every element as potentially holding text. There is no text here and SC 1.4.3 does not apply. What DOES apply is SC 1.4.11, and it was measured by hand: the filled bar reads 5.32:1 against the unfilled one, and the unfilled bar's outline reads 7.09:1 against the page. Both clear 3:1.
As above — an empty bar, not text. Filled vs unfilled measures 6.65:1, over the 3:1 SC 1.4.11 asks of a non-text indicator.
As above — an empty bar, not text. Filled vs unfilled measures 4.67:1, over 3:1.

Not a text pairing. `.ion-streaming-text__cursor` is an empty, aria-hidden <span> drawn as a block — deliberately not a text character, since some screen readers read a literal cursor glyph aloud. The gate pairs the paragraph's inherited colour against the cursor's background. Measured properly, the cursor is 7.09:1 against the page.

The same SC 1.4.3 exemption as --text-disabled on --surface-disabled, reached from the other direction. A disabled label declares a colour and no background of its own, so from 3 Sep 2026 it is measured against the three neutral grounds it could sit on. Muted is the darkest of them and the only one it falls short against. The criterion exempts text that is part of an inactive user interface component regardless of what is behind it, and raising this would work against the requirement that disabled controls look unavailable.
Same exemption as Light — SC 1.4.3 incidental text, inactive component.
SC 1.4.3 incidental text, inactive component — the same categorical exemption as Light. Listed per ground because a disabled label declares no background of its own and is measured against all three.
